newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's PDVSA refutes overproduction charge.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's PDVSA refutes overproduction charge.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) is not breaking OPEC production quotas and has to buy crude to meet its market, PDVSA President Luis Giusti said Tuesday.
"We have a market which is substantially larger than our own production," Giusti told reporters after a hearing in Congress.
PDVSA's total production, including about 230,000 barrels per day (bpd) of products and natural gas, is about 2.7 to 2.8 million bpd, Giusti said.
In addition, PDVSA buys between 200,000 and 300,000 bpd to meet its market, he added.
Venezuela is frequently cited by oil traders for flouting its 2.359 million bpd OPEC quota.

Reports that Venezuela produces over 3 million bpd appeared to be backed up by a PDVSA document obtained recently by Reuters which showed that the company saw its 1996 production averaging 3.14 million bpd with 2.727 million bpd exported.
Giusti declined to comment on the document.
